page.layout: One printed page, right of the gutter. Top: woodcut ornament band. Then title block centred (title, subtitle, small ornament), chapter heading, and running text in one column. Signature "A" centred at the foot. Left edge shows mirrored show-through and fragments of the facing page, not transcribed. Page number at top right corner.

main_text.head: ANTONII FAYI COMMENTARIUS IN LIBRUM SALOMONIS, QVI inscribitur Ecclesiastes.
CAPVT PRIMVM.
main_text.p: 1 VErba Ecclesiastæ, filij David, Regis in Ierusalaim.
2 Vanitas vanitatum, dixit Ecclesiastes: vanitas vanitatum,omnia vanitas.
3 Quid utilitatis est homini de vniuerso labore suo, quo laborat sub sole?
4 Generatio una labitur, & altera generatio aduenit:terra autem in seculum stat.
5 Et oritur Sol & occidit Sol, & ad locum suum regreditur vbi oritur.
6 Vadit ad Meridiem & circuit ad Aquilonem: subinde circumeundo pergit ventus, & ad circuitus suos reuertitur ventus.
7 Omnia flumina pergunt ad mare,&mare non impletur: ad locum vnde pergunt flumina, illuc reuertuntur vt rursus redeant.
8 Cuncta res laboriosa,nec potest vir eloqui: non satiatur oculus videndo, non expletur auris audiendo.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament band at head of page, not transcribed. Ornamental rule between title and chapter heading. The "A" centred at the foot is a signature. Marginal show-through from the facing page on the left edge is not transcribed. Headings were set in spaced capitals and italic in the original; the chapter-number "1" before verse 1 is a large decorated initial "V" joined to "Erba". Possible misreadings: "Aquilonem" and "Cuncta" are read from a faint scan.
